properties.scientific_name: Pinus sp. (recorded as Pinus ponderosa, unverified)
properties.origin: Unknown; P. ponderosa is from western North America
properties.id_tip: Count needles per bundle: 3 long flexible needles with orange jigsaw bark that smells of vanilla = ponderosa; 3 short stiff twisted needles and cones that stay on for years = pitch pine; 2 needles = Austrian or red pine; 5 stiff needles in a dense crown = Swiss stone pine.
properties.story: Ponderosa pine is the great yellow pine of the American West, with bark that smells like vanilla on a warm day. If this tree really is one, it is a rare easterner; if not, it is likely our own pitch pine or the map's Swiss stone pine.

properties.as_written: Red Maple - "Acer rubrum" (official map key, letter G)
properties.origin: Native to Massachusetts and eastern North America
properties.id_tip: Something is red in every season: red twigs and buds in winter, red flowers in March, red leaf stalks in summer, scarlet leaves in fall; leaves 3-lobed with toothed edges.
properties.story: Red maple is the most common tree in Massachusetts and the first to color in September. Look for red somewhere on it in every month of the year.
properties.season: fall color scarlet, March red flowers

properties.as_written: Hedge Maple - "Acer campestre" (official map key, letter H)
properties.origin: Europe and western Asia
properties.id_tip: Small tree with small 3-5 lobed leaves with rounded lobes, milky sap in the leaf stalk, corky ridged twigs, and seeds spread flat in a straight line.
properties.story: In England this little maple is clipped into farm hedges, which is where its name comes from. Its seeds spread out in a straight line like airplane wings, unlike any native maple.
properties.season: fall color yellow

properties.as_written: Swiss Stone Pine - "Pinus cembra" (official map key, letter J)
properties.notes_as_written: Section A, west edge near Main Street
properties.origin: Alps and Carpathians
properties.id_tip: Five stiff needles per bundle (white pine has soft ones), dense narrow column shape, orange-brown fuzzy young shoots, egg-shaped cones that never open and hold edible nuts.
properties.story: This slow-growing Alpine pine makes the pine nuts of the Alps, and its cones never open; birds called nutcrackers tear them apart and plant the seeds. It stays tidy and dense for decades, a perfect cemetery evergreen.
properties.season: year-round dense evergreen, purple-brown cones
